title: Design System: JBDC — The Atelier Ledger

display.purpose: A Design's name on the single-view empty plate.

title.purpose: History and New design titles, a Design's name on Detail and in the single view's panel, and a Library tile's name.

subtitle.purpose: The Detail and Edit headers, empty-state headings, second-order titles.

body-sm.purpose: Meta lines, secondary copy, muted values.

label.purpose: Field labels, button text, stage names, materials.

mono.purpose: Dates, ids, measurements, constants — data, not prose.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Resting cards, buttons, inputs, selects, the density switch, and the FAB's paper action rows — barely there.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: The centered dialog and alert, and the dropdown menus that open above the page — the deepest point in the system.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The create form's Select popup — one step shallower than the dialog, so a choice list reads as a list rather than a decision.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: Overlays, dialogs, and menus arriving; honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: The stage row opening and closing beneath the journey tabs.

motion.name: press
motion.value: instant tonal shift; card 0.98 dip + 5% ink wash held 120ms
motion.purpose: The press itself never animates; the held beat lets the Owner see it before the route opens. Edit's editable rows take the Kraft tint alone on the system press state, with no dip and no held timer.

motion.name: stage-tab-fill
motion.purpose: The journey rail's Deep Wood fill travelling to the chosen stage tab; honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: stage-tab-press
motion.purpose: A stage tab's content dipping on press; the fill never moves; honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: delete-swap
motion.purpose: The delete control's trash becoming the confirm word, inside the Quiet Turn budget; reduced motion resolves it on the spot.

motion.name: delete-press
motion.purpose: The delete control dipping on press, over its tonal wash; the one button allowed the dip because destruction answers in the hand; honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: section-mark
motion.purpose: Detail's wood rule and Edit's warm fill settling on the chosen section; honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: section-switch
motion.purpose: The incoming section when a Detail or Edit section tab is chosen, inside the Quiet Turn budget; honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: sheet-settle
motion.purpose: The floating sheet card settling at its content detent, inside the Quiet Turn budget.

motion.name: detail-arrival
motion.purpose: The Library's Detail route only; every other route keeps its default transition. Honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: stage-word
motion.purpose: The journey counter's stage name when the pager crosses into another stage. Honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: fab-rise
motion.purpose: The Library FAB's paper action rows opening. Honors Reduce Motion.

components.name: Paper Sheet
components.description: The sheet wrapper: a floating Unbleached Paper card inset 12px from the screen's sides and lifted above the bottom safe area, with all four corners at 16px. Every sheet wears an inset dashed frame in Faded Thread, 8px inside the card's edge, around a 24px body gutter that stands the content 16px clear of the frame; a sheet stacked above another steps one tone deeper (Kraft, then deep Kraft), so the stack reads as depth without a shadow. No sheet draws a drag handle. The header carries the title in the serif voice and one ghost X, labelled after its sheet. The same wrapper carries Edit's four sheets, each naming that X after itself — "Close category and collection", "Close add material", "Close material", "Close new material".

narrative.overview:
JBDC is one designer's private catalog of her own clothing designs, and the interface reads as her bound studio notebook: warm paper surfaces, a wood-toned accent for the things that matter, serif titles like specimen labels. The photography is the artwork; the chrome is the furniture around it. The feel is warm, unhurried, precise — a working archive, not a showcase.

The system is quiet archival. Depth comes from paper tonal steps and hairline borders, never from shadow play; press feedback is a tonal shift, not a bounce; motion is a short fade that honors the system Reduce Motion setting, with one small zoom-fade into a design's Detail. Color is spent on meaning only: Sanded Wood marks confirmed work and primary actions, Muslin Sage marks work in progress and active selection, Rejection Red marks what did not proceed. Everything else is paper and ink.

Photography has its own surfaces: the design pager's 3:4 black plate, the full-screen black image detail, and Kraft mounts where a cover is missing. The pager fits the whole image inside its stage. The paper world never floats over a photograph; the only thing allowed to blur is the single view's details panel, and it blurs only the cover beneath it. Chrome over a photograph is a translucent-black pill with white ink.
keyCharacteristics: Paper tonal hierarchy — Warm Paper page, Unbleached Paper cards, Kraft Layer mounts — instead of shadows; the Design detail alone inverts the mat, Unbleached Paper underfoot and Warm Paper for its cards
Cormorant Garamond titles over DM Sans body; DM Mono for dates, ids, measurements, constants
Two accents with fixed meanings: Sanded Wood (confirmed/primary/selection), Muslin Sage (in-development/active); red is rejection and destruction only
Hairline Thread Line borders everywhere; dashed frames are the signature for empty attach points and missing covers
Photography leads on fixed stages: a 3:4 inset journey pager that fits the whole image, 4:5 Library covers, 3:4 journey thumbs
Fades ≤ 200ms, honoring Reduce Motion; nothing bounces or loops

rules.name: The Ink-and-Paper Rule
rules.body: Color is state, not decoration. Wood = confirmed, primary, and selection; Sage = in-progress, active, and focus; Red = rejection and destruction. No third accent hue ever enters the system; everything else is paper and ink.

rules.name: The Overlay Exception
rules.body: Over photography, persistent chrome is a translucent-black pill (rgba(0,0,0,0.6)) with white text; muted text runs at 60% white, hairlines at 15%, fills at 10%, and unselected strokes at 40%. A menu or sheet the Owner deliberately opens may be paper; chrome that merely sits on the image may not. The same overlay tone is the scrim behind a sheet, and a dialog dims the page on 50% black; those scrims are the only black over paper.

rules.name: The Detail Ground Rule
rules.body: The Design detail is the one page that inverts the mat: Unbleached Paper underfoot, Warm Paper for its cards and stage tabs. No other screen changes ground, and the inversion is light and dark alike.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Cormorant speaks only for titles — the names of screens, designs, and dialogs. Anything the Owner reads as information is DM Sans; anything read as data is DM Mono. Cormorant body text is forbidden.

rules.name: The Flat-Archive Rule
rules.body: A surface's importance is read from its tone, never from its shadow. If a shadow exists at all it stays ≤ 5% black; glass effects, large blurs, and decorative drop shadows do not enter this system. A sheet opened above another takes one tone step deeper in light and one step lighter in dark, so the stack reads as depth in both appearances without gaining a shadow.

rules.name: The Single-View Carve-Out
rules.body: The single view's details panel is the one surface allowed to blur, and it blurs only the photography directly beneath it — a frost at intensity 50 over a 60% paper panel. No card, sheet, bar, menu, or control blurs; nothing blurred sits over a paper surface.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: Pills are for state and selection — badges, counters, toggles. Rectangles are for containers and controls. A pill never carries a sentence; a rectangle never carries a status.

rules.name: The Quiet Turn Rule
rules.body: Motion never announces — it only arrives and leaves, in 200ms or less. Every animation honors the system Reduce Motion setting with a crossfade or an instant cut.

dos: Do resolve every color through the slot table in Colors — wood is primary, sage is secondary, Kraft is muted/accent.
Do separate with Thread Line hairlines and group with one hairline box or a Kraft mount; let tone carry the hierarchy.
Do give every editable row one trailing pencil in Faded Thread and the Kraft press wash; Status carries neither.
Do mark every empty attach point with the dashed frame — an empty stage, a missing cover, an add action — and use Faded Thread when the frame must be read against Kraft.
Do keep Cormorant for titles only, DM Sans for information, DM Mono for dates, ids, and measurements.
Do put persistent chrome over photography in translucent-black pills with white ink, and keep persistent paper chrome off the photograph.
Do use fades of 200ms or less that honor the system Reduce Motion setting.
Do lay out inside safe-area insets and end every scroll in 48px of breathing room.
Do write empty and error states plainly, in sentence case, with one action — and name terminology from GLOSSARY.md.
donts: Don't introduce any accent hue beyond wood, sage, and red.
Don't lift a card with a shadow heavier than the 5% whisper; no glass, no gradients, no blur backdrops — the single view's details panel may blur only the photography beneath it.
Don't set a status in anything but a pill — never a rectangle, a banner, or a colored row.
Don't fill an empty stage with illustration or icon decoration; the dashed frame is the empty state.
Don't place persistent paper chrome on a photograph; use the translucent-black pill. Only a menu or sheet the Owner opens may be paper over an image.
Don't announce a save with a toast or a banner; History is a screen the Owner opens.
Don't animate an entrance longer than 200ms, or with a spring that bounces.
Don't add a second pure white or a black fill to the paper world; Warm Paper is its one white. Black is photography's ground and the scrim behind a sheet or dialog, never a paper surface.
